name: Complaints lodged
computation: Count of complaints created in the month across all live banks.
why: Volume context for every other metric. Not good or bad on its own.

name: Complaints on a 48-hour target
computation: Complaints whose target is 48 hours (complex issues, or extended by a team lead) ÷ complaints lodged.
why: Context for the target figure. A steady rise means more complex complaints, or targets being stretched.

name: Qualified leads
computation: New banks in the month that fit the target segment and agreed to a demo.
why: Earliest sign of future revenue; feeds pilots two to three months later.
if_worst: Founder calls to every federation contact; run one more federation workshop this month.

name: Pilot-to-paid conversion
computation: Pilots that signed a paid contract ÷ pilots that finished, to date.
why: Shows whether the free pilot proves enough value for a bank board to pay.
if_worst: Exit interview with each lost pilot; fix the top reason before starting new pilots.

name: Resolved within target
computation: Complaints resolved before their own target (24 or 48 hours from lodging) ÷ complaints resolved in the month.
why: Our core promise to bank customers and the main value a bank buys. Each complaint is measured against the target on its receipt.
if_worst: Review the slowest teams with each bank's Principal Nodal Officer; tune routing rules.

name: Median time to first action
computation: Median hours from lodging to the first staff note, status change or reply.
why: Leads the target figure: with no action for a sixth of the target (4 hours on 24, 8 on 48), a case escalates to the team lead.
if_worst: Officer refresher training; turn on a morning digest of untouched cases.

name: Lodged online
computation: Complaints lodged on the website ÷ all complaints, including the branch paper register.
why: Paper complaints bypass the clock and the report. This is real adoption by customers.
if_worst: Branch QR posters and SMS links in passbook updates; staff lodge walk-in complaints online.

name: Lodged through the AI assistant
computation: Complaints submitted after a chat with the AI complaint assistant ÷ complaints lodged online.
why: Shows whether less tech-savvy customers find the plain-language chat easier than the form.
if_worst: Test chat prompts in Hindi and Marathi; move the chat button above the form.

name: Weekly active officers
computation: Officers who signed in and acted on a case in the last 7 days ÷ officers with access.
why: If officers drift back to Excel, the product stops working for the bank.
if_worst: Customer success visit; check whether officers are doubling up in a spreadsheet.

name: Waiting for an officer
computation: Complaints that waited more than 15 minutes to be allocated to an officer ÷ complaints lodged.
why: Allocation is automatic. Waiting means a team has nobody on duty with room, so the clock runs with no owner.
if_worst: Review duty rosters and max-open limits with each bank; add a back-up officer per team.

name: “Where is my complaint” calls
computation: Calls to the branch or call centre asking for complaint status, % change against the bank's pre-launch month.
why: Fewer status calls is the saving a branch manager notices first.
if_worst: Make the tracking SMS link more prominent; add complaint status to the IVR menu.

name: Customer satisfaction
computation: Average of the 1–5 rating customers give after their complaint is resolved.
why: Fast but unhelpful replies show up here before they show up as Ombudsman cases.
if_worst: Read every 1 and 2 rating this week; share three examples with each bank.

name: Contracted ARR
computation: Sum of annual subscription value of all signed, active contracts at month end.
why: The headline measure of business size; the March 2027 target is ₹6 lakh or more.
if_worst: Shorten the sales cycle: a founding-bank discount that expires this quarter.

name: Paying banks
computation: Banks with a signed, paid contract at month end.
why: Revenue concentration: with few banks, losing one hurts a lot.
if_worst: Prioritise the two warmest pilots for conversion before starting new pilots.

name: Gross margin
computation: (Revenue − hosting − AI − SMS and email costs) ÷ revenue for the month.
why: Whether each new bank adds profit. Target is about 80%.
if_worst: Review AI and SMS spend per bank; move heavy users to the higher tier.

name: CAC payback
computation: Sales and marketing spend ÷ new banks, divided by monthly gross margin per new bank.
why: How fast a new bank pays back what it cost to win. Target is 6 months or less.
if_worst: Shift spend from events to federation and vendor referrals.

name: Logo churn (annualised)
computation: Banks that cancelled in the last 12 months ÷ banks at the start of the period.
why: The model only works if banks stay for years. Target is under 8%.
if_worst: Founder call to each cancelling bank; offer a 90-day recovery plan.

name: Days to collect payment
computation: Unpaid invoices at month end ÷ revenue billed in the last 90 days × 90.
why: Cooperative bank boards approve payments slowly. Cash, not ARR, pays salaries.
if_worst: Annual billing in advance with a 2% early-payment discount; invoice before board meetings.

name: Confidential details blocked
computation: Submissions where the guard stopped an OTP, PIN, CVV, card, Aadhaar or PAN number.
why: Shows the guard is working. A sharp rise can mean a wave of scam calls at a bank.

name: Confidential details stored
computation: Complaints found holding an OTP, PIN, card or Aadhaar number in the monthly audit sample.
why: One leak can end a bank relationship and draw RBI attention. Must stay at zero.
if_worst: Incident response: redact within 24 hours, tell the bank's DPO, fix the guard pattern, re-audit.

name: Contact reveals per case
computation: Logged views of customer contact details ÷ cases opened by staff.
why: Staff should reveal contacts only to resolve a case. A high rate suggests snooping.
if_worst: Send each bank its reveal log by officer; require a reason before a reveal.

name: AI routing overridden by staff
computation: AI routing decisions that staff changed ÷ all AI routing decisions.
why: High means the AI routes badly. Near zero over a long time can mean staff stopped checking.
if_worst: Retrain routing prompts on the overridden cases; fall back to rules only for weak services.

name: Duplicate or spam complaints
computation: Complaints marked duplicate or spam by staff ÷ complaints lodged.
why: Misuse of a free public form. Too many waste officer time and AI spend.
if_worst: Turn on CAPTCHA and mobile OTP for repeat lodgers.

name: Reopened or taken to the Ombudsman
computation: Resolved complaints reopened by the customer or escalated to the RBI Ombudsman ÷ complaints resolved.
why: Guards against officers closing cases early just to beat the 24-hour clock.
if_worst: Audit 20 quick closures per bank; count only accepted resolutions in the 24-hour figure.

name: Targets extended by team leads
computation: Complaints whose target a team lead moved from 24 to 48 hours ÷ complaints lodged.
why: Extending is allowed but logged and told to the customer. A high rate means leads are stretching the clock instead of fixing cases.
if_worst: Audit the extensions by lead; require a written reason; report the rate to the Principal Nodal Officer monthly.

name: Officer load spread
computation: Open complaints of the busiest officer in each team ÷ that team's average, averaged across teams.
why: Allocation should spread work evenly. A high spread means manual reallocation is piling cases on a few people.
if_worst: Check reallocations by lead; review max-open limits; rebalance in the weekly team meeting.

name: Open past RBI's 30 days
computation: Complaints still open more than 30 days after lodging, at month end.
why: RBI's legal deadline. Every one is a regulatory breach for the bank.
if_worst: Same-day call with the bank's Principal Nodal Officer; written reply within 48 hours.

name: AI cost per complaint
computation: Claude API spend for chat and routing ÷ complaints lodged.
why: Long-term viability: pricing assumes under ₹1 per complaint.
if_worst: Cap chat turns; reuse routing for repeat issue types; use a smaller model for routing.

name: Uptime
computation: Minutes the lodge, track and staff pages passed health checks ÷ minutes in the month.
why: A customer who can't lodge goes to the branch or straight to the Ombudsman.
if_worst: Post-incident review; add a status page and a standby database region.

name: Response time (95th percentile)
computation: 95th percentile time for database function calls from the site, in milliseconds.
why: Rural customers are often on slow mobile data; slow pages lose them.
if_worst: Profile the slowest functions; add indexes; trim the queue page payload.

name: AI assistant errors
computation: AI function calls that failed or timed out ÷ all AI function calls.
why: When AI fails the form still works, but routing falls back to rules only.
if_worst: Check API status and timeouts; add retry with backoff.

name: SMS and email delivered
computation: Notifications confirmed delivered ÷ notifications sent.
why: The reference number and updates reach customers only through these messages.
if_worst: Switch to the backup SMS provider; check DLT template approvals.

name: Escalation job delay
computation: Average minutes between when a case should escalate (a sixth, half and five-sixths of its target) or breach, and when it did.
why: Escalations are the safety net for the 24-hour target. A late job means late escalations.
if_worst: Move the job to a dedicated scheduler; alert if a run is skipped.
